EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
“Hurricane Katrina and Victims’ Labor-Market Outcomes, 1999–2009”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary design: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event‐study
extension and individual fixed effects.

Why DiD is appropriate  
• Exogenous, sharp, and well-timed shock (August 2005) => natural
  experiment.  
• Ten years of panel IRS data give multiple pre- and post-periods,
  allowing (i) validation of the parallel-trends assumption and
  (ii) dynamic treatment-effect estimation.  
• Individual identifiers let us absorb time-invariant person‐level
  heterogeneity and flexibly control for common year shocks.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
TREAT_i = 1 if the taxpayer’s 2004 mailing ZIP code is in a county
(FIPS) that FEMA classified as “catastrophic” (Categories IV & V
damage) when Katrina made landfall; 0 otherwise.

Control group (counterfactual)  
Three concentric definitions improve robustness:  
A. “Near-but-unhit” counties along the Gulf Coast that received only
   “limited/minor” FEMA damage codes.  
B. Inland counties (same states) at least 100 miles from the coast and
   with no Katrina‐related disaster declaration.  
C. Nationwide matched controls selected by propensity score on
   pre-2004 income, employment, and demographics.

Treatment timing  
POST_t = 1 for tax years ≥ 2005; 0 for 1999–2004.  
Event-time dummies k = −5,…,+4 give leads/lags in the event study.

No running variable/cutoff is required (not RDD).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of Katrina, treated and control
    taxpayers would have continued on similar earnings/employment
    paths.  
    – Testable via pre-2000-2004 event-study leads.

A2. No anticipatory effects: Households did not change labor-market
    behavior in 2004 because of Katrina expectations. Reasonable—the
    hurricane’s precise landfall and severity were unforeseeable.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): One person’s treatment does
    not affect another’s outcome in the control group. Plausible after
    focusing on geographically separated controls; we also test for
    spillovers.

A4. Composition stability: Differential mortality and out-migration do
    not mechanically drive the results. IRS data allow tracking SSNs
    across addresses, helping to retain movers and gauge attrition.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Selective migration after 2005  
    • Use “intent-to-treat” status based on 2004 address, keeping
      Katrina movers in the treated group.  
    • Check robustness to “as-treated” definitions using actual 2005
      residence.  
    • Re-weight by inverse probability of remaining in the panel.

T2. Differential economic trends in the Gulf unrelated to Katrina  
    • Include state-by-year fixed effects.  
    • Add controls for county-level oil prices and military spending
      shocks occurring in 2005–2006.

T3. Measurement error in residence (PO boxes, displaced filers)  
    • Cross-validate IRS ZIPs with USPS change-of-address files.  
    • Run sensitivity dropping taxpayers whose ZIP switched pre-2005.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R CODE OUTLINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE DiD
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load & merge data ----------------------------------------------
irs <- fread("irs_1999_2009.csv")           # raw return-level data
fema <- fread("fema_katrina_damage.csv")    # county-level damage

# 2. Variable construction ------------------------------------------
# keep one record per SSN–year (assume already)
setDT(irs)

# Attach county damage code
irs <- merge(irs, fema, by = "county_fips", all.x = TRUE)

# Treatment indicator based on 2004 residence
irs[, treat := (damage_cat %in% c("IV","V"))]   # 1/0 but NA outside Katrina area
# Freeze 2004 status
irs[, treat2004 := treat[year == 2004], by = ssn]
irs[, treat2004 := fifelse(is.na(treat2004), 0, treat2004)]

# Post dummy and event-time dummies
irs[, post := (year >= 2005)]
irs[, event_time := year - 2005]

# Person and year factors for FE
irs[, id := as.factor(ssn)]
irs[, yr := as.factor(year)]

# Outcome variables
irs[, lnincome := log(total_income + 1)]
irs[, employed := as.integer(wages > 0)]   # 1 if any W-2 income

# 3. Main DiD regression --------------------------------------------
did_inc <- feols(lnincome ~ treat2004*post |
                 id + yr,
                 data = irs,
                 cluster = ~county_fips)

summary(did_inc)

# 4. Event-study (dynamic DiD) --------------------------------------
# Interact treat with each event_time, omitting k = -1 as baseline
irs[, evt := factor(event_time)]
es_inc <- feols(lnincome ~ i(event_time, treat2004, ref = -1) |
                id + yr,
                data = irs,
                cluster = ~county_fips)

# Plot coefficients
coefplot(es_inc, title = "Event-study: Katrina effect on log income")

# 5. Robustness: placebo using 2001 "pseudo-event" ------------------
irs[, placebo_time := year - 2001]
placebo <- feols(lnincome ~ i(placebo_time, treat2004, ref = -1) |
                 id + yr,
                 data = irs[year <= 2003],   # pre-Katrina years only
                 cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(placebo)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts sizable short-run income and employment losses due to
job destruction and displacement, partially recovering over time.

Magnitude priors (treated vs. controls):  
• 2005–2006: –10 % to –15 % in real annual income; –5 pp employment.  
• By 2009: gap narrows to –3 % income; employment difference ≈ –1 pp,
  reflecting partial but incomplete convergence.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DiD)  (1 = satisfied, 0 = weak)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. Pre-treatment parallel trends ….. 1  
C2. No anticipatory behavior ……….…. 1  
C3. No contemporaneous shocks ……….. 0.5 (oil sector boom risk)  
C4. Stable composition / attrition … 0.5 (migration, mortality)  
C5. No interference (spillovers) ……. 0.5 (labor-market spillovers possible)

Total: 3.5 / 5 → “moderately strong” identification.
